1. Mapped all visual components from the whiteboard diagram and transcript to valid vocabulary items:
   - User icon mapped to UserConsumerWebMobile (representing mobile, web, TV, SMS users).
   - AWS WAF mapped to WAF.
   - Application Load Balancer mapped to ALB.
   - AWS Fargate mapped to Fargate.
   - MemoryDB Redis mapped to MemoryDB.

   - On-Premises system mapped to OnPremDC.
   - CloudWatch mapped to CloudWatch.
   - Kinesis Data Firehose mapped to Firehose.
   - S3 bucket mapped to S3.
2. Identified three main operational flows:
   - Flow 0: Session management originating from On-Premises editorial systems through VPN and Fargate backend to MemoryDB.
   - Flow 1: High-concurrency voting flow from users through WAF (geo-filtering), ALB, Fargate frontend, and MemoryDB (Lua scripts) back to users.
   - Flow 2: Monitoring and logging flow streaming logs from ALB/Fargate to CloudWatch, Firehose, and S3 storage.

graph.name: Mediaset Amici Voting Architecture on AWS
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, High-Throughput Voting System, Serverless
graph.notes: Architecture designed by Mediaset for handling spiky live TV show voting loads with latency under 10ms processing millions of votes.

nodes.name: Users
nodes.notes: Voters accessing via mobile apps, web, connected TVs, or SMS

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Validates user location to restrict voting to allowed regions (Italy)

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Distributes incoming web traffic to containerized application frontends

nodes.name: Fargate
nodes.notes: Runs separate frontend and private backend container services; handles authentication and business checks

nodes.name: MemoryDB Redis
nodes.notes: Stores active session state and contestant counters; processes vote logic using single-threaded Lua scripts (<10ms target)

nodes.name: VPN
nodes.notes: Secure tunnel connecting broadcast studio to private backend services in AWS

nodes.name: On-Premises
nodes.notes: Editorial control systems used to manage voting sessions and view real-time results

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Aggregates application and infrastructure logs for real-time operational dashboards

nodes.name: Data Firehose
nodes.notes: Streams log data continuously from CloudWatch to long-term storage

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores audit and certification log data for long-term retention

edges.notes: Editorial team sends session open/close commands
VPN routes session management commands to private Fargate backend service
Backend service initializes session state and contestant list in MemoryDB
WAF passes geo-verified traffic to load balancer
ALB routes voting request to frontend Fargate container service
Fargate executes Lua script on MemoryDB to process vote, update counters, and check limits
MemoryDB returns voting outcome and remaining quota back to Fargate
ALB sends access logs to CloudWatch
Fargate containers emit application logs to CloudWatch
CloudWatch streams logs into Kinesis Data Firehose
Firehose writes log stream to S3 bucket for long-term storage
